rationale: An official filing portal could publish llms.txt or agent-oriented docs, so this axis applies to California SOS. Direct probes found nothing: https://www.sos.ca.gov/llms.txt returns 404, the markdown docs variant returns 404, and the bizfile portal serves a bot-management shell instead of readable content to agents. No other evidence shows any agent-oriented documentation.

bizfile California is an online portal for filing, searching, and ordering business records, so an in-product AI insights or suggestions feature is a fair question for it. However, nothing in the evidence describes any AI-generated insights, recommendations, or assistant inside the portal. The documented features are standard filing, search, certificate ordering, and access-control functions.

The axis applies: a government business-filing portal could plausibly offer scheduled or recurring filings, or an API that users automate against. The evidence shows no such capability. Filings are manual online, mail or in-person submissions; no OpenAPI spec or llms.txt was found; the bizfile portal sits behind a bot-management shell; and from August 1, 2026, online Statement of Information filings will require entity-linked User Access accounts. The ballot-tracking notification is a voter alert, not a user-configured background automation.

A government online filing portal like bizfile California could plausibly ship a built-in AI assistant or chatbot, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence pack mentions any built-in AI assistant or delegated-task capability; the docs describe only conventional online filing, search, and ordering.

Automating a government filing service is a fair axis, but nothing in the evidence shows an API, CLI, or headless/CI path. All filing and search runs through the interactive bizfileOnline web portal. Probes found no OpenAPI spec, and the portal sits behind Incapsula bot management that serves an SPA shell even for robots.txt. The new User Access requirement explicitly gates online filings to authorized, entity-linked accounts. Bulk data files and a downloadable notary list are periodic data downloads, not a way to run the product headlessly.

The California Secretary of State's bizfile portal is a government business filing and records-search service with no agent or assistant, so plugging in MCP servers is a category error for this product type. Nothing in the evidence shows it ships any agent or tool-consuming capability that would make the axis apply.

Nothing in the evidence lists the full set of steps (account creation, credentials, identity-proofing) a founder must clear before formation or other filings. Missing for 10: an explicit published checklist of account, credential and identity-proofing requirements for formation filings; details of identity verification; confirmation that requirements are disclosed before the flow rather than discovered mid-flow; independent or hands-on corroboration.
